### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/vitest.config.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35cc663868de0ea06346b0087ac2d0222b9c5ed3`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/vitest.config.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35cc663868de0ea06346b0087ac2d0222b9c5ed3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b88696c39ecab682b4554f58c6c490aa817dcde4` — the merge of head `ba9ec457d95728754a39030bc4891e50327b6504` into base `35cc663868de0ea06346b0087ac2d0222b9c5ed3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b88696c39ecab682b4554f58c6c490aa817dcde4 && git checkout b88696c39ecab682b4554f58c6c490aa817dcde4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 35cc663868de0ea06346b0087ac2d0222b9c5ed3 ba9ec457d95728754a39030bc4891e50327b6504 && git checkout -B drift-repro 35cc663868de0ea06346b0087ac2d0222b9c5ed3 && git merge --no-ff ba9ec457d95728754a39030bc4891e50327b6504

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35cc663868de0ea06346b0087ac2d0222b9c5ed3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 35cc663868de0ea06346b0087ac2d0222b9c5ed3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Read at 2026-11-16T04:10Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6906919972; no lane request (owed per check-owed-reviews). Independence: implemented in a project thread for domain:server#5; reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Readers of the moved keys, in this repository: none at runtime.** `git grep` of the six `embedder_*` keys over `packages/`, `ui/`, `examples/` and `skills/` at the head finds only `ai.manifest.ts` (the declaration and its form-check handler), a comment in `visibility-eval.ts`, translations, tests and changelogs. No package calls `getNamespace('ai')`, `get('ai', …)` or `subscribe('ai', …)` for them, and none reads the `knowledge` namespace. `@objectstack/embedder-openai` takes constructor options, not settings. The one runtime reader is outside this repository (see ③).
- **What an undeclared key means at the head (read in `settings-service.ts`).** Declared keys are the registry's `scopes` map, built in `registerManifest` from the manifest's specifiers. With the section gone on a default boot: a write is refused (`UnknownKeyError`, 400 `UNKNOWN_KEY` at the door); an in-process `get` of one key throws the same error; `getNamespace('ai')` resolves declared keys only, so it answers without the six keys and without their defaults (`embedder_provider: none`, `embedder_batch_size: 64`); `OS_AI_EMBEDDER_*` overrides are no longer audited or served. Nothing in the diff deletes a row, and no boot path prunes rows of undeclared keys, so "stored values remain and return when the service is mounted" holds. The built-in `reset` action clears declared keys only (`resetNamespaceRows` walks the namespace payload). No settings export or import door exists in `service-settings` at the head, so that question has no subject.
- **Registration order: true.** `resolvePluginOrder` visits every `optionalDependencies` id that is composed before the plugin itself, and both kernels (`kernel.ts`, `kernel-base.ts`) order through it. The literal `com.objectstack.service.settings` equals `SETTINGS_PLUGIN_ID`, which is `SettingsServicePlugin.name`. That plugin registers its manifests, its action handlers and the `settings` service inside `init()`, so at the knowledge plugin's `init()` the `ai` page is already registered. No cycle: the settings plugin's only edge is the ObjectQL engine, and `service-settings` does not depend on `service-knowledge`. The contribution test mounts the knowledge plugin before the settings plugin, and the dev's A7 ablation (dependency dropped, 6 of 7 red) shows the order is carried by the declaration, not by `use` order.
- **Knowledge mounted without settings.** `contributeKnowledgeSettings` catches the missing service and returns with nothing offered, Setup entry included; the knowledge service itself is registered before the call. Read, not pinned by a test (N2).
- **Re-registering `ai`.** `registerManifest` replaces the entry and keeps the previous `actions` map, so `ai.test` survives the join; env-override reports are de-duplicated, so the second registration does not repeat them.
- **Setup entry and routes: one reading of "mounted".** The entry is registered by the same function, after the `knowledge` manifest, and only when a settings service took it. The static entry is gone from `SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS`. The label key stays in the platform-objects bundles, so the contributed entry is translated.
- **Translations.** All 11 locale bundles change the one string, `settings.ai.description`, the same way (no embedder, no knowledge base). No key moved or was removed: the `knowledge` page's copy and the embedder group's copy stay in the bundles, which is what the mounted deployment reads. The coverage test now measures the `ai` manifest with its embedder section joined and still enumerates `knowledgeSettingsManifest` from the manifests module, so it covers the same declarations as before; it is not weakened.
- **Pins: not vacuous.** The default-absent pin asserts by status and `error.code`, with a control per case (the `ai`, `storage`, `mail` namespaces present; `provider` key present; `nav_settings_ai` present; at least six embedder keys enumerated). The contribution suite compares a mounted kernel against a bare one built by the same function. The two corpus pins keep 10 manifests by adding the two moved declarations back explicitly. The dev's seven ablations each went red, and the one that first stayed green (A5) produced a new pin.
- **CLI pin and checklist.** `connect-agent-both-halves-wire.pin.test.ts` counts the Setup tree a composition without the knowledge service serves: 33 to 32, with an explicit `not.toContain('nav_settings_knowledge')`; correct for this change. The checklist JSON restates 9 builtins and 10 served namespaces with revision entries; `check-platform-checklist` is green in CI.
- **Lockfile.** Six added lines: the two workspace links `service-knowledge/package.json` adds. Nothing else.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the true arm, on both the PR body and the changeset: served doors now refuse on every deployment that does not mount the service. The `!` title, the **BREAKING** paragraph and the "What to do" paragraph are present.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: no schema key, accepted value or metadata type moves; a settings manifest is a runtime registration and the `SettingsManifest` schema is untouched. So the level is `patch` on each package the diff moves, and the changeset names exactly those three (`service-settings`, `service-knowledge`, `platform-objects`). `packages/cli` changes a test only and publishes nothing.
- ADR-0087: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the fitting category. No export is retired (`knowledgeSettingsManifest` and `builtinSettingsManifests` both remain, the former now also on the package entry), so the runtime-export category has no subject, and with `none` declared the narrowed-kind refusal of this exemption does not apply.
- `Skills-docs: none` is true: `git grep` under `skills/` at the head finds no `embedder_` key, no settings-page URL for knowledge, no `builtinSettingsManifests` and no `nav_settings_*` id.
- CI on this head: 72 check-runs, all completed; 61 success, 11 skipped, none failed, none running.

CI completed before posting: 72 check-runs on this head, 61 success, 11 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open dependency, not closed by this PR: the hosted embedder binding.** The cloud lane's answer (6902349823) is that the hosted runtime does not mount `service-knowledge` and its AI plugin reads `ai.embedder_*` through `getNamespace('ai')` on every boot. Per ① that read answers without the six keys once this lands, so the hosted embedder would be configured from nothing, silently. The seat already parked the PR as a draft, `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/cloud#4569` (6906109461). This PASS judges the diff; it is **not** a statement that the PR may land. Landing waits for cloud#4569 to merge, or for the cloud lane to say the binding no longer reads those keys; if cloud keeps the binding, this PR needs a fallback and a new review.
- The dev's report carries no open question. Its two out-of-scope notes (checklist count; the cloud reader) are both answered: the first in this diff, the second above.
- Surface deviations named by the dev (package entry exports, vitest aliases, the two corpus pins) are all required by the approved dependency and are read above. The `packages/cli` pin is a further file outside the listed surface, added in the last commit; it is a count the change makes false, so it belongs here.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or in-app join is added.
- Acceptance 3 is met by the test kernel, as the area decision (6898471166) ruled; `examples/app-todo` is unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes a refusal real rather than taking a working capability away from an in-repository consumer: the two pages configured a service no stock deployment mounts, and the maintainer ruled that they be hidden everywhere. The mechanism follows the precedent already in the tree (the branding entry lives with its namespace). The diff agrees with the ruling and with the code it cites.

S1 (should-fix) — `contributeKnowledgeSettings` recognises "the bundled `ai` page" by its key set alone and then registers `withAiEmbedderSection(aiSettingsManifest)`, the bundled declaration. A host that passed its own `ai` manifest with the same keys and different declarations is therefore not "left untouched", which is what the PR body, the changeset and the function's comment claim. Either make the recognition match the claim or narrow the claim, and pin the host-manifest branch (untouched, warning logged) and the already-declares-embedder branch, neither of which has a test. Detail is in the seat's private notes. Not a must-fix: no deployment mounts the service today, and the branch needs a hand-built `ai` manifest.

S2 (should-fix) — the changeset's "What to do" says stored values stay, and stops there. It should also tell an operator who stored a value under the two retired pages and wants it gone what to do, since the default deployment no longer serves the doors that edit those keys. A changeset sentence is enough. Detail is in the seat's private notes.

N1 (nit) — the page and its Setup entry are still titled "AI & Embedder" in every locale on a deployment that now shows no embedder section. The card's acceptance names the page by that title and asks only for the section and the description, so this is residue, not a miss; a follow-up card can decide whether the title travels with the section.

N2 (nit) — "knowledge mounted with no settings service offers nothing and does not throw" is read in the code and stated in the changeset, with no test.

N3 (nit) — the PR body names `f27aef7db8` as the final head and lists no `packages/cli` change; the head is `ba9ec457d9`, one test commit later. The body's Verification section should say so.

No must-fix. Should-fix: S1, S2.
